title:	Tell agents to read Trunk Check CI logs instead of running trunk locally
state:	OPEN

--
## Why
When Trunk Check fails on a PR, agents try to reproduce it by running `trunk check` locally. In cloud sandboxes this is slow and can get killed (on PR #195 it exited with 137), and local results can differ from CI. The CI log already lists every finding with file, line, rule and whether it is auto-fixable.

## What would help
Add guidance to `CLAUDE.md` (near "Landing PRs") saying:

- When Trunk Check fails, read the failed job log first: `gh run view <run-id> --log-failed`.
- Fix the listed findings by hand, or with the repo's own formatter and linter (`ruff format`, `ruff check`).
- Run `trunk check` locally only if the log is not enough, and not in memory-limited sandboxes.
- Check the PR branch for bot fix commits (for example Pullfrog) before pushing, to avoid duplicate work and rejected pushes.

## Related
Found while fixing PR #195.

The change should target `AGENTS.md` (it's what Pullfrog and Claude load as the repo guide). A `CLAUDE.md` symlink/pointer is optional if Claude Code-specific discovery is wanted. **Plan** (docs-only, one file): 1. In `AGENTS.md` under `## Landing PRs`, add a short "When the Trunk Check gate fails" block after the queue-mechanics bullets (~line 113, before the "The queue gates on…" paragraph), with the issue's four bullets refined: - Read the failed job's log first: `gh run view --log-failed`. The "Trunk Check" job (`.github/workflows/trunk-check.yml`) lists every finding with file, line, rule, and auto-fixability; the gate is file-diff scoped, so only touched files are reported. - Fix findings by hand or with the tool matching the linter that reported them. For Python that's ruff, but its config lives only in `.trunk/configs/ruff.toml` — use `ruff check --config .trunk/configs/ruff.toml ` / `ruff format --config .trunk/configs/ruff.toml `; bare `ruff format`/`ruff check` don't mirror CI. Non-Python findings (pyrefly, actionlint, vale, …) need their own tools, so the wording shouldn't imply ruff covers everything. - Run `trunk check` locally only if the log is insufficient, and never in memory-limited sandboxes — it runs the full toolchain and can be OOM-killed (exit 137, as hit on PR #195). - Before pushing, fetch the PR branch and check for bot fix commits (e.g. Pullfrog) to avoid duplicate work and rejected pushes. 2. Verification: `AGENTS.md` is covered by the Trunk gate's general markdown linters (markdownlint-cli2, prettier, markdown-link-check); Vale is scoped to `docs/**` only. A one-file PR is validated by the "Trunk Check" gate itself; no docs-site regeneration is involved. input.command:
python3 - <<'E'
p='AGENTS.md'
s=open(p).read()
m="The queue gates on the statuses in"
add="""### When Trunk Check fails

- Read the failed job log first: `gh run view <run-id> --log-failed`. It lists
  every finding with file, line, rule and whether it is auto-fixable.
- Fix the findings by hand, or with the tool that reported them. For Python,
  use `ruff format --config .trunk/configs/ruff.toml <path>` and
  `ruff check --config .trunk/configs/ruff.toml <path>`; bare `ruff` does not
  pick up the repo config. Other linters need their own tools.
- Run `trunk check` locally only if the log is not enough, and never in
  memory-limited sandboxes (it can be killed with exit 137).
- Before pushing, fetch the PR branch and check for bot fix commits (for
  example Pullfrog) to avoid duplicate work and rejected pushes.

"""
assert s.count(m)==1
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(m,add+m))
E
